text:
John Tavares came back from injury into the worst stretch of Toronto's season, and he has been the one facing the cameras for it. After the sixth straight home loss he apologized to fans, a moment that travelled far beyond Toronto. Tuesday in Chicago he scored his first point since returning. The Mississauga native, now 36 and with 1,185 career points before this season, has been a Leaf since 2018.

The numbers on him are mixed. His own chances are still good (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best forwards at getting to the front of the net last season), but Toronto has just 36% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five with him on the ice, 13 points worse than without him. Some of that is the team around him: the Leafs have scored 6.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, which usually swings back.

His minutes are down a bit and Heavy.com is running headlines about fans wanting him and Auston Matthews gone. Watch whether his line can at least break even on chances.
